speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Since its establishment, Kwong Wai Shiu has played an important role in providing quality care to patients in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: It has expanded the scope of its services significantly over the years, and currently operates a nursing home, a senior care centre, a Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) Centre, and provides home care services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Demand for healthcare services is expected to grow as a result of Singapore's rapidly ageing population.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Not only do we need to add capacity, especially in the Intermediate and Long Term Care (ILTC) sector, we will need to also build up strong providers to deliver affordable, quality care.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Service providers like Kwong Wai Shiu will have an increasingly important role to play in serving needy patients and leading the way to innovative solutions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: To better position itself to meet the future challenges, Kwong Wai Shiu is expanding its capacity and capability.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Kwong Wai Shiu is doubling its capacity at its current Nursing Home with the redevelopment and expansion of its facility at this site.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: The new Nursing Home, which will also house a Senior Care Centre, will be completed later this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Kwong Wai Shiu's upcoming Active Ageing Hubs in the vicinity of its current Nursing Home will also support our seniors to age in place.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: The Active Ageing Hub is a new concept we are trying out as part of the Action Plan for Successful Ageing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: It is a one-stop centre for our seniors, where they can participate in active ageing programmes, and receive care services at the same place if needed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: The centre can also provide assisted living services, such as housekeeping and grocery shopping, to seniors living nearby.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: As Kwong Wai Shiu enhances its services and infrastructure to cater to the changing health needs of our population, it will also need to keep up with the times and ensure the hospital is well-positioned to support its mission to serve all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: It is thus timely for Kwong Wai Shiu to review its organisational framework, which is currently set out in the Ordinance, and modernise its corporate and governance structure.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: The Kwong Wai Shiu management, therefore, sought the Ministry of Health's (MOH's) support to repeal the Ordinance and establish the hospital as a Company Limited by Guarantee (CLG) similar to other voluntary welfare organisations (VWOs), for the following reasons.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: First, the current Ordinance has not been substantively amended since its enactment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: As a result, its provisions have become antiquated and are impeding Kwong Wai Shiu's development and growth as a modern healthcare provider.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: For example, before Kwong Wai Shiu can dispose of any immovable property, it is currently required to first seek the leave of the High Court and serve the application on the Attorney-General.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: This unduly hampers Kwong Wai Shiu's ability to efficiently manage and control its assets and property to respond to the changing needs of Singapore and ensure that the hospital's activities remain relevant and viable.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: In comparison, assets of modern charities and Institutions of a Public Character (IPCs) are usually governed by their boards, and these charities and IPCs are not required to routinely obtain the leave of the High Court and to serve the application on the Attorney-General when disposing of their immoveable property.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Another example is the requirement for Kwong Wai Shiu to follow the Chinese lunar calendar for the submission of its accounts to the "Secretary of Chinese Affairs", a position which no longer exists today.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Second, the Kwong Wai Shiu management wanted to improve and strengthen KWSH's overall governance and corporate accountability framework.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: The Ordinance is not fully compatible with the guidelines recommended in the Code of Governance for Charities and IPCs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: For example, the Ordinance does not include guidelines pertaining to board governance, as well as the avoidance of conflicts of interests.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: As a CLG, Kwong Wai Shiu will be governed by a constitution which contains such guidelines.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: This will ensure that Kwong Wai Shiu will continue to operate in a sound manner and assure its donors and members and the public that its funds and assets are responsibly managed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Last, and most fundamentally, the Ordinance limits the scope of Kwong Wai Shiu's operations and beneficiaries.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: In reality, Kwong Wai Shiu has gone beyond this limited scope and has long been serving the general public, regardless of race, religion and dialect.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: The breadth of Kwong Wai Shiu's current activities is worthy and welcome, and it is opportune that the formal limitations imposed by the Ordinance are removed in support of its noble and beneficial activities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: The Kwong Wai Shiu Bill will allow Kwong Wai Shiu to modernise and strengthen its corporate structure and provide flexibility in managing its assets and operations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: The CLG, named "Kwong Wai Shiu Hospital", was incorporated last year and has been registered as a Charity and obtained IPC status as of 18 July 2016.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: The Commissioner of Charities, and specifically, MOH as the Sector Administrator for healthcare charities and IPCs, have been identified as the supervisory regulatory authority for Kwong Wai Shiu.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: The new CLG will be governed by the Companies Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: A board of directors will oversee the management of the CLG.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: As a result of the modernisation, Kwong Wai Shiu will have greater flexibility to expand its charitable activities, thereby further benefiting the broader community and public.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: The transfer will take place after the Kwong Wai Shiu Bill comes into force.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: This includes staff employment − the continuity of the staff's employment, and the terms and conditions of their service, will not be affected by the transfer to the CLG.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Likewise, Kwong Wai Shiu's rights, powers, duties and liabilities as an employer will be transferred to the CLG.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: As such, the Kwong Wai Shiu Bill will not have any adverse impact on Kwong Wai Shiu's employees.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Kwong Wai Shiu has also engaged its union, the Manual and Mercantile Workers' Union, and I understand that the union is supportive of the new corporate structure.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Kwong Wai Shiu has also engaged its internal stakeholders, including employees and board members.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: I would also like to highlight that the hospital's operations will not be affected and patients are unlikely to experience any inconvenience or any adverse changes as a result of the transition.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: I hope that Members will support the Bill.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mdm Speaker, the KWSH was established in 1910 and already has 106 years of history.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: KWSH provides affordable healthcare services to those with chronic conditions regardless of race or religion, supplements the Government's healthcare policy and is an important charitable organisation in the private sector.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: During the colonial times, a group of Cantonese businessmen founded KWSH.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: They provided free hospitalisation and clinical consultation for Cantonese immigrants and looked after the poor and needy clansmen.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Although 100 years have gone by, times have changed and Singapore has already gained Independence for more than 50 years, the content of this legislation had never been amended.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: I met up with Mr Patrick Lee, Chairman of KWSH, and its senior management to get a better understanding of the situation.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: After listening to them, I was deeply moved.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Being a large IPC, the hospital's operations have already fulfilled the conditions required of an IPC.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: It gave the board more confidence in making long-term development plans.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: There are many other charitable hospitals of this kind.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Motivated by passion, regardless of race or religion, they provide long-term nursing care for the elderly and the more vulnerable groups of people, and demonstrate the merits of an inclusive society.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: I am really pleased to note the Government's support for KWSH.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: With our rapidly ageing population, more and more elderly people require care.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: KWSH is in the process of trying out something new, to help the elderly grow old amidst familiar surroundings.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: With the joint effort of the Government and the private sector, KWSH will enter a new phase of development.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: MOH gives great support to the hospital in terms of its policies and regulations, while the hospital's management team will be unified in dedicating financial resources and energy in the expansion.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: This spirit of moving ahead with the times is exemplary and should be emulated by many social groupings and charitable organisations.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: The operational capital of these charitable hospitals relies on donations from society, and I earnestly hope that every member of society could continue to support the hospital.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: This successful experience could be replicated in other areas.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Due to changed circumstances, the original objective behind establishing many civic organisations has changed significantly.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: In particular, for some trade associations, the entire industry has to undergo restructuring.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: I hope that more Government agencies and trade associations could be inspired by the example of KWSH and enable more moving stories to be written.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mdm Speaker, just as my Parliament colleague has just mentioned, KWSH, has cared for many low-income families since its establishment in 1910.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The hospital provided Singaporeans with good medical services and contributed much in terms of charitable and healthcare services.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: When it started, it provided both TCM and western medicine services, a first for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In the early days, it also provided maternity services and treated communicable diseases.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am glad to see that the hospital has evolved its services over time.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Today, it operates a nursing home, a day rehabilitation centre, a TCM centre and provides homecare services.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I understand that it is even going out into the community to provide healthcare talks and mobile health screening for the elderly.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: KWSH has always played an important role in caring for the indigent.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Even today, nursing home residents who are unable to foot their bills can still receive funding from KWSH's charity funds.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Thinking about the hospital brings back many vivid memories.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: When I was young, like many other residents, I visited the clinics there for treatment.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: KWSH's low fees have benefited me, my family and my neighbours.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am glad to see that the Government has decided to keep the hospital and allow it to continue to do charitable work and help the low-income families.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am very happy to see that, and I am also very touched.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Although in the early days, the hospital's main purpose is to care for immigrants coming from Kwong-Chau, Wai-Chau and Shiu-heng prefectures of the Canton Province of China, in fact, it has also already been caring for people from other dialects or races.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Even though I am not a Cantonese, I am a Hokkien, I have also benefited from the hospital.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Whilst it serves all Singaporeans, KWSH has also had the special support of the Chinese community.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The hospital has many volunteers helping them in their programmes.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The volunteers add much warmth and friendship to the lives of the hospital's residents.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: They chitchat with the residents, share stories and sing songs with them, just like in a kopitiam.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Even though KWSH's Ordinance was outdated, it has been able to achieve all this.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I note that the Ordinance is not fully compatible with the guidelines recommended in the Code of Governance for Charities and IPCs.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While KWSH had earlier made the right decision to broaden its scope of services to patients regardless of race, language or religion, it is appropriate that the mandate of the hospital, as reflected in its governing document, be updated in line with our national values.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Moving forward, I hope KWSH will contribute even more to healthcare services in Singapore following the repeal of this Ordinance.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am glad that the Government has supported the upgrading of the hospital though part of it is affected by the land acquisition for development.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The upgraded hospital will help support our ageing population and patients with chronic diseases.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The hospital has an important role to play and I hope it will continue to receive support from the public.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I would also like to take this opportunity to thank our seniors, the Pioneer Generation and the public for their support over the years, with which KWSH is able to make continual success in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As it transitions into the next phase of its development, I am heartened to see that it continues to serve the public in the spirit of charity.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As I learn about its makeover to be reopened as Singapore's largest nursing home, I am assured of our Government's focus on our elderly, and to ensure that they are being well cared for.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I was impressed by the amount of effort and planning put in to ensure that it is not just any nursing home, but one which bucks the trend and sets higher standards for all new nursing homes in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand MOH has funded the expansion of the KWSH.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Thirdly, referring to clause 4(1) which states that the trustees and committee members have been involved in the hospital's operation for many years, building up valuable relationships with stakeholders, will they still be able to contribute after leaving or will they be invited to serve on the new board?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand that KWSH is unique in its approach.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For example, it will be a one-stop shop for services ranging from TCM to specialised wards to treat dementia.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is also not gated and members of the public can enter freely to use its services.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: There will be other innovative functions, such as a "haze management zone" and a "memory street" on every floor to help the elderly retain their memories.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is an excellent step forward in the design of nursing homes, and I hope that all new nursing homes will also model this approach.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I also understand from nurses on the ground that one of the key issues faced is the lack of available beds for patients with higher acuity of care in nursing homes.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Another category of patients is those undergoing haemodialysis.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Many have been rejected by nursing homes, and families find it difficult to cope as there are few options available.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I hope this issue would be taken into consideration and new nursing homes will be able to accommodate those with acute conditions as well.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: (In Mandarin):   Mdm Speaker, first, let me thank Mr Thomas Chua, Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Mr Louis Ng who have expressed their appreciation to KWSH for its contribution to healthcare in Singapore and voiced their support of the Bill.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Indeed, KWSH has played an important role in developing our healthcare system.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As one of Singapore's oldest charitable healthcare institutions, KWSH has cared for the sick and needy for more than 100 years since it was established.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: It has continuously developed and evolved its services to cater to Singaporeans' healthcare needs.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In the early days, KWSH responded to national needs by providing maternity services and treating communicable diseases, such as Tuberculosis, and even continued its operations during the Japanese occupation.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: To ensure that it could care for Singaporeans regardless of race, language or religion, KSWH also went beyond its Ordinance and opened its doors to all Singaporeans in 1974.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In recent years, KWSH started to provide additional services, such as speech therapy, cancer rehabilitation and home care.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I understand that KWSH also actively engages the community through mobile health screening, public health talks, and active ageing programmes.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As mentioned by Mr Thomas Chua, KWSH has been innovating to help seniors age well in a familiar environment.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The Active Ageing Hubs that I earlier mentioned, is a good example of KWSH's efforts.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In addition, Kwong Wai Shiu is also collaborating with the Academy of Chinese Medicine (ACMS ) to provide better care services for the elderly.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: ACMS will be part of Kwong Wai Shiu's new integrated hub concept to provide better TCM services, and to more Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This platform pulls together several streams of services, including the TCM clinic, to support seniors with varying needs and help them to stay well within the community.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Kwong Wai Shiu and ACMS will also jointly work on research study and training programmes to benefit clients and the TCM industry.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As mentioned by Mr Gan Thiam Poh, it is to Kwong Wai Shiu's credit that they have managed to adapt over time despite being constrained by its antiquated Ordinance.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I commend the Kwong Wai Shiu leadership for having the foresight to look ahead and push for these changes to their corporate structure so that they are able to move more quickly and confidently to meet future challenges.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: MOH is happy to support them in these efforts.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The Members have also raised various comments and questions on the Bill.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I was heartened to hear Mr Gan Thiam Poh's affirmation of Kwong Wai Shiu's efforts in helping patients in need over the years.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Indeed, Kwong Wai Shiu has a team that evaluates cases submitted by medical social workers.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Those who are assessed to be in need will be assisted using Kwong Wai Shiu's charity funds.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Apart from helping indigent patients, I understand that Kwong Wai Shiu also caps its nursing home inpatient fees to ensure that they remain affordable for Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This is also why it is important for Singapore to have VWO care providers.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: They have a passion to serve and can harness the joint resources of the community to help patients in need.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Kwong Wai Shiu has promised me that it will continue to fulfil its mission of providing healthcare services to the sick and poor in Singapore regardless of race, language or religion, and serving the community with passion.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I am confident that they will be able to fulfil their objective of serving the community for the next 100 years.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: (In English): Mdm Speaker, Mr Louis Ng queried how the new entity will be funded and operated.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: He also asked for clarifications on how the transfer of employees from the existing Kwong Wai Shiu entity to the new entity will take place.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In line with this, Kwong Wai Shiu's employees will simply become employees of the new entity, with their employment terms unchanged.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I am glad that Mr Louis Ng raised the question on whether Kwong Wai Shiu's trustees and committee members will still be able to contribute to Kwong Wai Shiu after the transfer to the new entity.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Kwong Wai Shiu's trustees and committee members have been closely involved with its operations for many years and contributed significantly to its strong track record in community service.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I understand from Kwong Wai Shiu that the trustees and committee members have been invited to serve on the new board and that most have agreed to do so.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Lastly, I would like to thank Mr Louis Ng for his suggestion to consider the possibility of nursing homes accommodating patients with higher care needs.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: MOH is currently looking into this and we will share more details in future.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The Kwong Wai Shiu Bill will modernise Kwong Wai Shiu's corporate structure and put Kwong Wai Shiu in a stronger position to respond to future challenges.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: At the same time, Kwong Wai Shiu will also have greater flexibility to continue providing quality healthcare services to Singaporeans.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 4.30 pm.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 4.08 pm until 4.30 pm.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: The Kwong-Wai-Shiu Free Hospital has also expressed its support for the Bill.
